core_obligations: Set up the reduction (proof lines 5682-5713): choose a scheme U with a surjective etale morphism to X; restriction along U gives a functor on modules that has both adjoints, hence commutes with all limits and colimits, and a module on X is quasi-coherent exactly when its restriction to U is, by the detection criterion.

Properties (1) to (4) (proof lines 5717-5745): for direct sums, arbitrary colimits, kernels and cokernels of morphisms, and short exact sequences the restriction to U commutes with the operation in question and the resulting restricted objects are quasi-coherent by the scheme case, so the same holds before restriction; the two-out-of-three property is inherited because restriction preserves short exactness.

Properties (5) and (6) (proof lines 5747-5768): the restriction of a tensor product is the tensor product of the restrictions, and the restriction of the internal hom into a module of finite presentation is the internal hom of the restrictions because restriction is a localization and internal hom commutes with localization; in both cases the scheme case applies to the restriction and the detection criterion transports the conclusion back.
proof_roadmap: Choose an etale cover by a scheme and record that restriction commutes with limits and colimits and detects quasi-coherence.
For each of the four additive properties, use the commutation of restriction and the scheme case.
For tensor products and internal homs, use the commutation with localization and then the detection criterion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the category of quasi-coherent sheaves on an algebraic space is stable under arbitrary direct sums and colimits, under kernels and cokernels, satisfies the two-out-of-three property for short exact sequences, and is stable under tensor products and under internal homs with a finitely presented first argument (statement lines 5657-5680). The proof (proof lines 5682-5772) reduces to the case of schemes by choosing a surjective etale cover and using that restriction commutes with all limits and colimits and detects quasi-coherence, then verifies the six properties by the corresponding identities for the restriction functor. H2: a reduction followed by six verifications, written out in full.
